The '''Ōshikōchi no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (凡河内国造; also rendered as ''Ōshikōchi Kokuzō'', ''Ōshikawachi no Miyatsuko'', or ''Ōshikawachi no Kokuzō'') were the [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial chieftains) who ruled over the Ōshikōchi Province.

== Overview ==

=== Names ===
The ''[[Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'' ("Kokuzō Hongi" chapter) records this clan as the '''Ōshikōchi no Kuni no Miyatsuko'''; alternative written forms include '''Ōshikawachi no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' and '''Ōkawachi no Kuni no Miyatsuko'''.

=== Ancestors ===
* According to the ''[[Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'' "Kokuzō Hongi," during the reign of [[Emperor Jinmu]], '''Hikokosohori no Mikoto''' (彦己曽保理命) was appointed as kuni no miyatsuko.
* According to volume 1 of the ''[[Kojiki]]'', [[Amatsuhinane no Mikoto]] is recorded as the founding ancestor of the Ōshikawachi no Kuni no Miyatsuko.

=== Clan ===
The clan was known as the '''Ōshikawachi clan''' (凡河内氏; ''[[kabane]]'' rank: ''Atai'' (直)). In the 12th year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (683), they received the ''muraji'' rank; in the 14th year, the ''imiki'' rank; and some members were later also granted the ''sukune'' rank.

== Base of operations ==
The western part of [[Settsu Province]] or the central part of [[Kawachi Province]].

=== Territory ===
The kuni no miyatsuko's domain corresponded to the region then called ''Ōshikōchi Province'', which later became [[Kawachi Province]], [[Izumi Province (classical Japan)|Izumi Province]], and [[Settsu Province]]. However, within this territory, multiple ''agata'' (sub-provincial districts) coexisted under various ''agata nushi'' (district chiefs) — including the Mino, Chinushika, Ina, Shiki, Konguchi, and Mishima ''agata'' — so the domain was not precisely identical to those three later provinces.

As they controlled the area of present-day [[Osaka Bay]], they are believed to have administered the [[immigrant|immigrant population]] (''toraijin'') and to have played an active role in diplomacy for the [[Yamato court]].

== Clan deity ==
Possibly '''[[Kawachi Kunitama Shrine]]'''.

=== Associated shrines ===
* [[Ikasuri Shrine]]
*: A ''shikinaisha'' (Engishiki-listed shrine) in Osaka City, Osaka Prefecture, claiming to be the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (foremost shrine) of Settsu Province. The Watanabe family who serve as its hereditary shrine priests (''shake'') are descendants of the Ōshikawachi Sukune line.

== Descendants ==
* [[Ōkawachi no Ajiharu]]
*: A powerful local chieftain (''gōzoku'') of the [[Kofun period]]. According to tradition, he was punished for refusing to present lands to [[Emperor Ankan]].
* [[Ōshikōchi no Mitsune]]
*: A poet of the [[Heian period]] and one of the [[Thirty-six Poetry Immortals]]. Together with [[Ki no Tsurayuki]], he was one of the principal poets of the ''[[Kokin Wakashū]]''.
* [[Hiromine clan]]
*: The hereditary shrine-priest family (''shake'') of [[Hiromine Shrine]] in [[Harima Province]].
